subject: Post-call: latency vs QPS tradeoffs — FastCommerce pilot next asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fastcommerce.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency vs QPS tradeoffs — FastCommerce pilot next asks

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the concrete asks so we can line up the right pilot: 

1) Goal: real-time pricing and checkout recommendations for mobile shoppers (sub-100ms tail for interactive flows, but bulk re-reranking acceptable at higher latency for batch workflows).
2) Traffic shape: 1.2M uniq daily users; peak session QPS estimated at ~1400 req/s with bursts up to 2.2k for flash sales. Typical generation size is ~45 tokens; embeddings used for similarity ops are separate.
3) Data posture: customer data must remain in their VPC for PCI scope; they want an isolated environment for any PII handling.

Given that, primary question is: do we recommend Hosted API (fast onboarding, flexible autoscale) or Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool + predictable tail latency)? Quick summary of our POV below and the pieces we need from your side to finalize a recommended pilot path.

Our POV (high level):
- If strict 99.9th percentile tail <100ms for the critical checkout path is non-negotiable at 2k burst QPS, Dedicated capacity or a Private deployment is the safer recommendation.
- If you can accept a small window (100–200ms) for tail under the very highest bursts and prefer faster time-to-live plus lower upfront commitment, Hosted API with configured autoscale + prefix caching is feasible for the pilot.
- Hybrid approach: start with Hosted for baseline production and move sensitive PCI flows into Dedicated or Private VPC when ready.

Action items we need from you to finish sizing and a formal Pilot SOW:
- Clarify which flows must be sub-100ms versus which can accept up to 200ms.
- Confirm concurrency per session (how many parallel model calls per user).
- Share a 24-hour QPS histogram or sample traffic CSV (timestamps + endpoint + avg tokens).

Next steps I propose: we draft a 4-week pilot that demonstrates both approaches: a Hosted baseline to validate model outputs and a short Dedicated smoke test on a reserved node to validate tail latency. Ben will attach a short perf snapshot with recommended node sizing and an initial SOW.

Happy to jump on another 30-min call early next week once you send the QPS sample.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:21:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency vs QPS tradeoffs — FastCommerce pilot next asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming: checkout personalization must target 95–99.9th percentile under 100ms for the cart UI (that’s the priority); product recommendations (browse) can be <=250ms.

Concurrency: average user session does ~1.6 parallel calls (cart + recommendations). During flash sales, we hit multi-region bursts where edge pop routing may be helpful.

I can export a 24-hour sample from our traffic logs — will share tomorrow. Also attaching our compliance team’s initial requirements; they will want to see network diagrams and KMS integration options.

Alicia
Head of Product
FastCommerce

Subject: Dedicated smoke sizing + perf snapshot (draft)

Alicia / Marissa —

Per the ask, attached is a quick perf_snapshot.csv and a one-pager of expected behavior. High level:
- For 2k burst QPS with sub-100ms tail we recommend a small dedicated pool sized to absorb burst (suggested: 4 x A100 80GB equiv with continuous batching and KV cache enabled). That config should keep 99.9th < 120ms for the majority of requests; true sub-100ms will depend on request distribution and token counts.
- Hosted API with autoscale + prefix caching: cheaper and faster to deploy, expected p95 around 60–90ms for 45-token requests; p99 will vary under sustained bursts.

Attachments included: perf_snapshot.csv (CSV)

Let me know if you want me to convert this into a short pilot SOW with acceptance criteria.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
